question: Recently, a Ukrainian military unit was named ‘Heroes of the UPA’ (Ukrainian Insurgent Army). UPA was an armed formation directly responsible for a genocide of citizens of the Second Republic of Poland, known as the Volhynia Massacre, in which over 100 000 Poles were cruelly murdered in 1943 and 1944.

Glorifying formations responsible for ethnic cleansing and mass atrocities clearly goes against the fundamental values of the European Union, such as respect for human dignity, human rights and the pursuit of historic truth and reconciliation.

As a candidate country to the European Union and recipient of unprecedented financial and military assistance from EU institutions, Ukraine should be required to comply with European standards, including stopping the national idolisation of criminals. Given the above: 1.
Is the Commission monitoring cases of institutional glorification of a formation responsible for a genocide against Poles, and does it intend to officially respond to this scandal?

Will the Commission consider the issue of historical revisionism, including the idolisation of UPA and the blocking of the exhumation of murdered Poles, in its assessment of Ukraine’s compliance with the political criteria necessary for membership of the European Union?

Is the Commission considering introducing conditionality mechanisms that would make the disbursement of further instalments of macro-financial assistance to Ukraine conditional on stopping the idolisation of individuals and organisations responsible for the genocide of citizens of current EU Member States?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.8.2026) The Commission assesses compliance of Ukraine with the accession criteria on the basis of the established framework, including the political criteria relating to the stability of institutions guaranteeing democracy, the rule of law, human rights and respect for and protection of minorities.

The Commission reports regularly on Ukraine’s progress in the context of the enlargement process. EU budget support and macro-financial assistance to Ukraine are governed by Regulations (EU) 2026/4671 and 2024/7922, requiring the fulfilment of a political precondition on upholding democracy, rule of law, and human rights, including those of persons belonging to minorities.

Ukraine Facility disbursements also depend on the fulfilment of Ukraine Plan steps, including reforms to align with EU rules, values and standards. Issues pertaining to historical interpretation, remembrance policies and commemorative practices are matters to be addressed in a spirit of dialogue, responsibility and good relations with neighbours.

The Commission encourages all efforts aimed at dialogue, reconciliation, and the respectful commemoration of all victims. As regards exhumations and related bilateral matters, the Commission encourages continued cooperation and dialogue between Ukraine and Poland, with a view to achieving tangible progress based on mutual respect and historical reconciliation.
1 Regulation (EU) 2026/467 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 February 2026 implementing

enhanced cooperation on the establishment of the Ukraine Support Loan for 2026 and 2027: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2026/467/oj. 2 Regulation (EU) 2024/792 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 29 February 2024 establishing the Ukraine Facility: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/792/2026-02-27.
